sentences.text: Sebecus was a terrestrial, meat-eating crocodylomorph that lived in South America, distinguished by a deep, narrow snout and unusual ziphodont dentition where teeth were laterally compressed and serrated.
Postcranial remains indicate the animal measured between 2.2 and 3.1 meters in length and weighed between 52.2 and 113.5 kilograms.
The postcranial skeleton remained largely unknown until Pol et al. (2012) described remains including a partially articulated specimen MPEF-PV 1776.
The Eustachian tubes featured several interconnected branches similar to those seen in crocodilians.

The genus has been placed in various positions within metasuchian crocodyliforms, and recent analyses suggest Sebecosuchia is polyphyletic with Sebecus forming a metasuchian clade distantly related to Notosuchia.

Fossils range from the Paleocene to the Mid Eocene, with possible records extending to the Late Miocene or Early Pliocene, covering the Danian to Zanclean epochs from approximately 66 to 3.6 million years ago.
A 2007 study reclassified S. huilensis and S. querejazus into separate genera, Zulmasuchus and Langstonia, respectively, after Paolillo and Linares assigned them to new groups.
